transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-14
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Laura Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Rajesh Singh (MarinerPay CTO), Maya Patel (Head of ML), Tom Brenner (Infra)

Summary:
Short discovery focused on Dedicated capacity for MarinerPay: reserved GPUs, isolation requirements, burst strategy, scaling expectations, and security controls (KMS, SSO). Agreed to run a benchmark pilot and share detailed traffic and token estimates.

Topics: Dedicated capacity, reserved nodes, VPC/private deployment, burst capacity/overflow, autoscale and canary rollouts, SOC2/KMS/SSO, telemetry and cost breakdowns.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Laura: Hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Laura from Redwood, we also have Diego from our SE team. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Rajesh: Good, thanks. We're excited, trying to, um, figure out a dedicated setup for inference for payments fraud and customer mentions, so, a bit high level today.
[00:18] Diego: Great. Quick agenda — understand current stack, isolation and security needs, throughput and latency SLOs, and then talk about dedicated sizing and burst patterns.
[00:27] Maya: Sounds good. For context we process about 10M requests a day but token-wise it's, uh, roughly 150M tokens daily, spikes to 1.5k QPS during peak hours.
[00:40] Tom: Our infra is on AWS, VPC-based, we need private networking and control plane access via our VPC peering or transit gateway.
[00:50] Laura: Got it. So sounds like you have production scale. Are you evaluating hosted or dedicated primarily?
[00:55] Rajesh: We started with hosted for experiments but need isolation and predictability — so Dedicated or Private. Key is reserved GPUs and ability to burst when campaigns hit.
[01:10] Diego: On Redwood Dedicated we offer reserved GPU pools — you can commit to a set of nodes (e.g., 3x A100s) with guaranteed capacity and a burst pool for overflow. Burst can be either shared capacity in our multi-tenant pool or you can reserve extra nodes for scheduled bursts.
[01:30] Maya: How does the burst work — is it automatic? We can't have huge latency variability for fraud decisions.
[01:38] Diego: You can configure policy-based burst. For latency-sensitive routes we recommend kept warm nodes and smaller batch sizes. Our routing can prefer reserved nodes first and then fallback to burst nodes with SLO-aware routing; if you need absolute isolation during peaks you'd reserve additional nodes for peak windows.
[01:55] Rajesh: What's the typical cold start or rewarm time for GPU-backed workers if we spin up burst nodes?
[02:02] Diego: If we provision a new node from scratch it's minutes — 3-5 typically, but with reserved burst nodes in a warm state we can keep them ready and that reduces rewarm to under 30s. We also support pre-warming heuristics based on traffic patterns.
[02:16] Tom: We need to understand autoscaling — we don't want scale to blow out cost during a DDoS spike or bug. Any guardrails?
[02:23] Laura: We support autoscale policies with max caps, token-level quotas, and circuit-breakers. Also can set fallback routes to cheaper model variants or to hosted fallback with lower QPS.
[02:34] Maya: Ok on models — are you running customer models only or do you host open models too? We plan to bring our fine-tuned Llama variant.
[02:42] Diego: Both. You can pin model versions on the Dedicated cluster. We support open models and custom ones; we handle quantization/optimizations during model onboarding and will benchmark throughputs for your model.
[02:55] Rajesh: How about KV cache and stateful sessions — our conversational fraud flow uses KV cache heavily for session context.
[03:03] Diego: We support persistent KV cache on Dedicated. There are options for local fast cache per node and a shared cache layer; we can discuss tradeoffs — shared cache helps across nodes but has latency overhead.
[03:17] Rajesh: Security — we need SOC 2, SSO/SAML, RBAC, KMS for keys, and audit logs retained for 1 year. Can Redwood support that in Dedicated or only in Private?
[03:30] Laura: Dedicated supports SOC 2 compliant controls, SSO/SAML, RBAC, and can integrate with your KMS. Audit logs and retention windows are configurable; Private on-prem gives you full control but Dedicated can meet most enterprise requirements. We'll share our security pack.
[03:44] Tom: On networking — do you require opening outbound to Redwood control plane? We prefer minimal egress.
[03:50] Diego: For Dedicated we have a customer-managed VPC peering option so the control plane can talk over a private link. There is a small control-plane handshake but data plane for inference can stay within your VPC depending on deployment.
[04:03] Maya: Cost — what's unit economics look like for reserved A100s vs hosted?
[04:08] Laura: Reserved capacity is priced at a commit level monthly; per-token costs drop materially because of utilization and batching. We'll send a model showing effective $/1M tokens for different configs. Also Optimize tooling suggests batch sizes and quantization to reduce costs.
[04:22] Rajesh: We want to run a benchmark with our real traffic — what's Redwood's approach to benchmarking?
[04:27] Diego: We run a customer benchmark on Dedicated: you provide sample payloads and traffic shape, we instrument latency and throughput, KV hit rates, and populate a cost/latency tradeoff matrix. Usually takes 1-2 weeks to run and iterate.
[04:40] Maya: For the benchmark we also need how you'll emulate burst windows for holiday traffic.
[04:44] Diego: We can replay your traces or synthetic ramp tests. We'll ensure peak QPS and token sizes are represented.
[04:50] Rajesh: What about canary deploys and rollouts — we need to test new model versions safely.
[04:55] Laura: Console supports canary and A/B rollouts, automatic fallback rules if regression is detected, and per-route dashboards. You can pin routes to specific model versions.
[05:05] Tom: Any constraints on multi-GPU model parallelism for large models? We plan to run a 30B model in 8-bit quant.
[05:12] Diego: We support tensor-parallel and pipeline-parallel setups depending on model topology. For a 30B 8-bit variant we typically recommend 2-4 A100s depending on perf targets. We'll size during onboarding.
[05:25] Maya: Encryption at rest — HSM/KMS integration? We need customer-managed keys.
[05:30] Laura: Yes, Dedicated integrates with customer KMS/HSM for key management. You can bring your own keys and we log key usage.
[05:38] Rajesh: Ok can you give an example config for our spikes? We're seeing baseline 800 QPS with 1.5k QPS peaks for 20-minute windows.
[05:46] Diego: Example config — baseline 3x A100 reserved nodes handling steady-state; two warm burst nodes for peak windows with pre-warming enabled; autoscale policy limit to +2 nodes but with circuit breaker to cap cost; route latency SLO 200ms P95, for which we'd use smaller batching on critical routes.
[06:05] Laura: We'll put together a recommendation spreadsheet with cost and perf estimates for 3, 4, and 5-node configs.
[06:12] Maya: What's the SLA for Dedicated?
[06:15] Laura: We have SLA tiers; standard Dedicated includes 99.9% uptime for reserved capacity and priority on support and capacity scheduling. Higher SLA tiers are available.
[06:25] Rajesh: Data residency — our data must stay in us-east-1. Can you guarantee region pinning?
[06:30] Diego: Yes, Dedicated can be provisioned in a specific region. For Private you'd have even more control but Dedicated can be region-isolated.
[06:38] Tom: Integration and deployment timeline? If we sign a pilot, how soon to get nodes live?
[06:43] Laura: For Dedicated pilot we usually do 2-4 weeks: contract, infra network setup (VPC peering), model onboarding and a benchmark run. We can accelerate if your legal and security uploads are quick.
[06:55] Rajesh: Legal — we need DPA and standard terms.
[06:58] Laura: Will include DPA; I'll loop Legal.
[07:02] Diego: Quick note, there might be slight word mislabels in the transcript: —
[07:06] Maya: (laughs)
[07:08] Laura: Ok let's talk topology specifics — do you want Full private control plane or Redwood-managed control plane with private data plane?
[07:15] Rajesh: Prefer private control plane if supported, otherwise managed with VPC peering is acceptable.
[07:20] Diego: Both options available. Private gives you more isolation and no third-party managed control plane, but it increases setup time.
[07:28] Maya: Observability — we need token-level cost, per-route P95, and anomaly alerts.
[07:33] Laura: Console provides token-level breakdowns, per-model dashboards, and you can send metrics to your datadog or prometheus endpoints.
[07:42] Tom: One more — can we import our SSO directory and sync groups to control who deploys models?
[07:47] Diego: Yes SAML/SCIM provisioning supported.
[07:50] Rajesh: Great. What's next?
[07:52] Laura: Next steps recap — I'll send pricing and the recommended 3-node and 5-node configs, Diego will send benchmark plan and infra checklist, and you (Maya) will share sample traffic and token estimates. We'll aim to schedule pilot kick-off week of 2026-04-27.
[08:10] Maya: Sounds good. Thanks.
[08:12] Laura: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with docs and links.
